answer: Sybil farms need one machine per identity, so admission is priced in silicon. Each applicant submits a TPM quote with a per chip endorsement key, and a verifier named QuoteRegistry refuses keys on file, so a cloned seat dies at the gate. The penalty trigger is an endorsement ban: a duplicate quote voids the bond and burns the stake. A fake needs a thirty five dollar board, a thirty POA bond and twenty minutes setup, so N fakes cost N times that sum; a gale of signups cannot outrun shipping, a falcon cannot carry two keys, and the canyon between hardware and software blocks bulk entry.
